reason: The giant previously redirected icy bodies outward, so following its influence on them addresses the first goal.
expectation: The giant may redirect some icy bodies inward, though their precise paths are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This could follow the leftover fragments, but I chose to investigate the ice first.

effect: The giant sent some icy bodies inward, opening several paths to follow them.
reaction: The different possible destinations make me curious about what happens to their ice.
reason: Following the icy bodies into warm space directly explores what happens as they approach the star.
expectation: Some ice may turn to gas in the warmer region, though the bodies may not all behave alike.

alternatives.reason: An encounter with the rocky world could also reveal the ice's fate, but I want to follow the warming first.

effect: Warming releases gas and embedded dust, while a cold remnant can remain; the ice's other paths are still open.
reaction: The immense, thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking contrast.
reason: An encounter with the moon-bearing world follows another possible fate of the inward-bound ice.
expectation: Some icy bodies may strike the world and leave material there, though the outcome is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Following the rocky fragments in warm space also addresses the remaining matter goal, but I want to explore the icy bodies first.

effect: The icy impacts cratered the world, vaporized ice and completed the ice goal without guaranteeing an ocean. I can now follow the rocky fragments.
reaction: The distinction between delivering ice and making an ocean was a useful surprise.
reason: Following fragments into warm space addresses what becomes of matter that missed the worlds.
expectation: The fragments may remain as debris or break into smaller pieces in the inner system; their fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments could also encounter the giant's rings, but I chose to follow them through the inner system first.

effect: Collisions turned some leftover stones into fine dust, opening a way to combine it with material released from warming ice.
reaction: The gradual breakdown into dust makes the fragments' fate clear.
reason: Combining the two dust sources follows matter that missed the worlds and may advance the remaining goal.
expectation: The released gas and dust may mix with the collision dust in warm space, though their longer-term fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The fragments could also affect the giant's rings, but the newly available dust combination brings both histories together.

effect: The two dust sources mingled and scattered starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to bring the two paths together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining dust from warming ice and colliding stones brought both histories together in a faint glow between worlds.

leastWorthwhile.text: Breaking leftover stones into dust was clear but less surprising than the other outcomes.

surprise.text: Icy impacts made craters and vaporized ice, but did not guarantee an ocean.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt clearly purposeless; the offered compatible options made the paths easy to follow, though I did not discover their compatibility myself.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow how the scattered material evolves, especially after seeing its different origins converge.
